clauses.title: Introduction
clauses.text: Introduction

clauses.title: Purpose of the secure coding checklist
clauses.text:
This technology agnostic document defines a set of general software security coding practices, in a checklist
format, that can be integrated into the software development lifecycle. Implementation of these practices will
mitigate most common software vulnerabilities.

clauses.title: Cost benefits of building secure software
clauses.text:
Generally, it is much less expensive to build secure software than to correct security issues after the
software package has been completed, not to mention the costs that may be associated with a security
breach.

clauses.title: Application security threat trends
clauses.text:
Securing critical software resources is more important than ever as the focus of attackers has steadily moved
toward the application layer. A 2009 SANS study1 found that attacks against web applications constitute
more than 60% of the total attack attempts observed on the Internet.

clauses.title: Assess development maturity and provide security validation capabilities
clauses.text:
When utilizing this guide, development teams should start by assessing the maturity of their secure software
development lifecycle and the knowledge level of their development staff. Since this guide does not cover
the details of how to implement each coding practice, developers will either need to have the prior
knowledge or have sufficient resources available that provide the necessary guidance. This guide provides
coding practices that can be translated into coding requirements without the need for the developer to have an
in depth understanding of security vulnerabilities and exploits. However, other members of the development
team should have the responsibility, adequate training, tools and resources to validate that the design and
implementation of the entire system is secure.

clauses.title: Glossary location
clauses.text:
A glossary of important terms in this document, including section headings and words shown in italics, is
provided in appendix B.

clauses.title: Software Security and Risk Principles Overview
clauses.text: Software Security and Risk Principles Overview

clauses.title: Overview of security principles
clauses.text:
Building secure software requires a basic understanding of security principles. While a comprehensive
review of security principles is beyond the scope of this guide, a quick overview is provided.

clauses.title: Software security goals and guide scope
clauses.text:
The goal of software security is to maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
resources in order to enable successful business operations. This goal is accomplished through the
implementation of security controls. This guide focuses on the technical controls specific to mitigating the
occurrence of common software vulnerabilities. While the primary focus is web applications and their
supporting infrastructure, most of the guidance can be applied to any software deployment platform.

clauses.title: Risk factors and exploitation example
clauses.text:
It is helpful to understand what is meant by risk, in order to protect the business from unacceptable risks
associated with its reliance on software. Risk is a combination of factors that threaten the success of the
business. This can be described conceptually as follows: a threat agent interacts with a system, which may
have a vulnerability that can be exploited in order to cause an impact. While this may seem like an abstract
concept, think of it this way: a car burglar (threat agent) goes through a parking lot checking cars (the
system) for unlocked doors (the vulnerability) and when they find one, they open the door (the exploit) and
take whatever is inside (the impact). All of these factors play a role in secure software development.

clauses.title: Development and attacker perspectives on software behavior
clauses.text:
There is a fundamental difference between the approach taken by a development team and that taken by
someone attacking an application. A development team typically approaches an application based on what it
is intended to do. In other words, they are designing an application to perform specific tasks based on
documented functional requirements and use cases. An attacker, on the other hand, is more interested in what
an application can be made to do and operates on the principle that "any action not specifically denied, is
allowed". To address this, some additional elements need to be integrated into the early stages of the
software lifecycle. These new elements are security requirements and abuse cases. This guide is designed to
help with identifying high level security requirements and addressing many common abuse scenarios.

clauses.title: Limitations of client side security controls
clauses.text:
It is important for web development teams to understand that client side controls like client based input
validation, hidden fields and interface controls (e.g., pull downs and radio buttons), provide little if any
security benefit. An attacker can use tools like client side web proxies (e.g. OWASP WebScarab, Burp) or
network packet capture tools (e.g., WireShark) to analyze application traffic and submit custom built
requests, bypassing the interface all together. Additionally, Flash, Java Applets and other client side objects
can be decompiled and analyzed for flaws.

clauses.title: Sources of security flaws throughout the software lifecycle
clauses.text:
Software security flaws can be introduced at any stage of the software development lifecycle, including:
• Not identifying security requirements up front
• Creating conceptual designs that have logic errors
• Using poor coding practices that introduce technical vulnerabilities
• Deploying the software improperly
• Introducing flaws during maintenance or updating

clauses.title: Potential scope of software vulnerability impacts
clauses.text:
Furthermore, it is important to understand that software vulnerabilities can have a scope beyond the software
itself. Depending on the nature of the software, the vulnerability and the supporting infrastructure, the
impacts of a successful exploitation can include compromises to any or all of the following:
• The software and its associated information
• The operating systems of the associated servers
• The backend database
• Other applications in a shared environment
• The user's system
• Other software that the user interacts with

clauses.title: Secure Coding Practices Checklist
clauses.text: Secure Coding Practices Checklist

clauses.title: Input Validation
clauses.text: Input Validation:

clauses.title: Validate data on trusted systems
clauses.text: • Conduct all data validation on a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Classify data sources and validate untrusted data
clauses.text:
• Identify all data sources and classify them into trusted and untrusted. Validate all data from untrusted
sources (e.g., Databases, file streams, etc.)

clauses.title: Centralize input validation
clauses.text: • There should be a centralized input validation routine for the application

clauses.title: Specify input character sets
clauses.text: • Specify proper character sets, such as UTF-8, for all sources of input

clauses.title: Canonicalize data before validation
clauses.text: • Encode data to a common character set before validating (Canonicalize)

clauses.title: Reject input when validation fails
clauses.text: • All validation failures should result in input rejection

clauses.title: Validate after UTF-8 decoding
clauses.text:
• Determine if the system supports UTF-8 extended character sets and if so, validate after UTF-8
decoding is completed

clauses.title: Validate all client data before processing
clauses.text:
• Validate all client provided data before processing, including all parameters, URLs and HTTP header
content (e.g. Cookie names and values). Be sure to include automated post backs from JavaScript,
Flash or other embedded code

clauses.title: Restrict request and response headers to ASCII
clauses.text: • Verify that header values in both requests and responses contain only ASCII characters

clauses.title: Validate data from redirects
clauses.text:
• Validate data from redirects (An attacker may submit malicious content directly to the target of the
redirect, thus circumventing application logic and any validation performed before the redirect)

clauses.title: Validate expected data types
clauses.text: • Validate for expected data types

clauses.title: Validate data ranges
clauses.text: • Validate data range

clauses.title: Validate data lengths
clauses.text: • Validate data length

clauses.title: Validate input against allowed characters
clauses.text: • Validate all input against a "white" list of allowed characters, whenever possible

clauses.title: Apply additional controls when allowing hazardous characters
clauses.text:
• If any potentially hazardous characters must be allowed as input, be sure that you implement
additional controls like output encoding, secure task specific APIs and accounting for the utilization
of that data throughout the application . Examples of common hazardous characters include:
< > " ' % ( ) & + \ \' \"

clauses.title: Check null bytes, newlines, and path alteration characters
clauses.text:
• If your standard validation routine cannot address the following inputs, then they should be checked
discretely
o Check for null bytes (%00)
o Check for new line characters (%0d, %0a, \r, \n)
o Check for “dot-dot-slash" (../ or ..\) path alterations characters. In cases where UTF-8 extended
character set encoding is supported, address alternate representation like: %c0%ae%c0%ae/
(Utilize canonicalization to address double encoding or other forms of obfuscation attacks)

clauses.title: Output Encoding
clauses.text: Output Encoding:

clauses.title: Encode output on trusted systems
clauses.text: • Conduct all encoding on a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Use standard tested encoding routines
clauses.text: • Utilize a standard, tested routine for each type of outbound encoding

clauses.title: Contextually encode untrusted data returned to clients
clauses.text:
• Contextually output encode all data returned to the client that originated outside the application's trust
boundary. HTML entity encoding is one example, but does not work in all cases

clauses.title: Encode characters unless safe for the interpreter
clauses.text: • Encode all characters unless they are known to be safe for the intended interpreter

clauses.title: Sanitize untrusted output to SQL, XML, and LDAP queries
clauses.text: • Contextually sanitize all output of un-trusted data to queries for SQL, XML, and LDAP

clauses.title: Sanitize untrusted output to operating system commands
clauses.text: • Sanitize all output of un-trusted data to operating system commands

clauses.title: Authentication and Password Management
clauses.text: Authentication and Password Management:

clauses.title: Require authentication for nonpublic pages and resources
clauses.text: • Require authentication for all pages and resources, except those specifically intended to be public

clauses.title: Enforce authentication on trusted systems
clauses.text: • All authentication controls must be enforced on a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Use standard tested authentication services
clauses.text: • Establish and utilize standard, tested, authentication services whenever possible

clauses.title: Centralize authentication controls
clauses.text:
• Use a centralized implementation for all authentication controls, including libraries that call external
authentication services

clauses.title: Separate authentication logic and redirect through centralized controls
clauses.text:
• Segregate authentication logic from the resource being requested and use redirection to and from the
centralized authentication control

clauses.title: Fail securely in authentication controls
clauses.text: • All authentication controls should fail securely

clauses.title: Secure administrative and account management authentication
clauses.text:
• All administrative and account management functions must be at least as secure as the primary
authentication mechanism

clauses.title: Store strong salted password hashes and restrict credential writes
clauses.text:
• If your application manages a credential store, it should ensure that only cryptographically strong one-
way salted hashes of passwords are stored and that the table/file that stores the passwords and keys is
write-able only by the application. (Do not use the MD5 algorithm if it can be avoided)

clauses.title: Hash passwords on trusted systems
clauses.text: • Password hashing must be implemented on a trusted system (e.g., The server).

clauses.title: Validate authentication after all data is entered
clauses.text:
• Validate the authentication data only on completion of all data input, especially for sequential
authentication implementations

clauses.title: Use identical authentication failure responses
clauses.text:
• Authentication failure responses should not indicate which part of the authentication data was
incorrect. For example, instead of "Invalid username" or "Invalid password", just use "Invalid
username and/or password" for both. Error responses must be truly identical in both display and
source code

clauses.title: Authenticate sensitive connections to external systems
clauses.text:
• Utilize authentication for connections to external systems that involve sensitive information or
functions

clauses.title: Encrypt and protect external service credentials
clauses.text:
• Authentication credentials for accessing services external to the application should be encrypted and
stored in a protected location on a trusted system (e.g., The server). The source code is NOT a secure
location

clauses.title: Transmit authentication credentials only through HTTP POST
clauses.text: • Use only HTTP POST requests to transmit authentication credentials

clauses.title: Encrypt transmission of non-temporary passwords
clauses.text:
• Only send non-temporary passwords over an encrypted connection or as encrypted data, such as in an
encrypted email. Temporary passwords associated with email resets may be an exception

clauses.title: Enforce password complexity requirements
clauses.text:
• Enforce password complexity requirements established by policy or regulation. Authentication
credentials should be sufficient to withstand attacks that are typical of the threats in the deployed
environment. (e.g., requiring the use of alphabetic as well as numeric and/or special characters)

clauses.title: Enforce password length requirements
clauses.text:
• Enforce password length requirements established by policy or regulation. Eight characters is
commonly used, but 16 is better or consider the use of multi-word pass phrases

clauses.title: Obscure password entry
clauses.text:
• Password entry should be obscured on the user's screen. (e.g., on web forms use the input type
"password")

clauses.title: Disable accounts after repeated invalid login attempts
clauses.text:
• Enforce account disabling after an established number of invalid login attempts (e.g., five attempts is
common). The account must be disabled for a period of time sufficient to discourage brute force
guessing of credentials, but not so long as to allow for a denial-of-service attack to be performed

clauses.title: Apply authentication controls to password resets and changes
clauses.text:
• Password reset and changing operations require the same level of controls as account creation and
authentication.

clauses.title: Use reset questions supporting sufficiently random answers
clauses.text:
• Password reset questions should support sufficiently random answers. (e.g., "favorite book" is a bad
question because “The Bible” is a very common answer)

clauses.title: Send email resets only to preregistered addresses
clauses.text:
• If using email based resets, only send email to a pre-registered address with a temporary
link/password

clauses.title: Expire temporary passwords and links promptly
clauses.text: • Temporary passwords and links should have a short expiration time

clauses.title: Require temporary password changes on next use
clauses.text: • Enforce the changing of temporary passwords on the next use

clauses.title: Notify users of password resets
clauses.text: • Notify users when a password reset occurs

clauses.title: Prevent password reuse
clauses.text: • Prevent password re-use

clauses.title: Require minimum password age before changes
clauses.text:
• Passwords should be at least one day old before they can be changed, to prevent attacks on password
re-use

clauses.title: Enforce password change schedules with administrative control
clauses.text:
• Enforce password changes based on requirements established in policy or regulation. Critical systems
may require more frequent changes. The time between resets must be administratively controlled

clauses.title: Disable password remember me functionality
clauses.text: • Disable "remember me" functionality for password fields

clauses.title: Report previous account use at successful login
clauses.text:
• The last use (successful or unsuccessful) of a user account should be reported to the user at their next
successful login

clauses.title: Monitor password attacks across multiple accounts
clauses.text:
• Implement monitoring to identify attacks against multiple user accounts, utilizing the same password.
This attack pattern is used to bypass standard lockouts, when user IDs can be harvested or guessed

clauses.title: Change default credentials or disable associated accounts
clauses.text: • Change all vendor-supplied default passwords and user IDs or disable the associated accounts

clauses.title: Reauthenticate users before critical operations
clauses.text: • Re-authenticate users prior to performing critical operations

clauses.title: Use multifactor authentication for sensitive transactional accounts
clauses.text: • Use Multi-Factor Authentication for highly sensitive or high value transactional accounts

clauses.title: Inspect third party authentication code for malicious code
clauses.text:
• If using third party code for authentication, inspect the code carefully to ensure it is not affected by
any malicious code

clauses.title: Session Management
clauses.text: Session Management:

clauses.title: Use only server or framework session identifiers
clauses.text:
• Use the server or framework’s session management controls. The application should only recognize
these session identifiers as valid

clauses.title: Create session identifiers on trusted systems
clauses.text: • Session identifier creation must always be done on a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Use vetted algorithms for random session identifiers
clauses.text:
• Session management controls should use well vetted algorithms that ensure sufficiently random
session identifiers

clauses.title: Restrict session cookie domain and path
clauses.text:
• Set the domain and path for cookies containing authenticated session identifiers to an appropriately
restricted value for the site

clauses.title: Fully terminate sessions on logout
clauses.text: • Logout functionality should fully terminate the associated session or connection

clauses.title: Provide logout on all protected pages
clauses.text: • Logout functionality should be available from all pages protected by authorization

clauses.title: Establish short session inactivity timeouts
clauses.text:
• Establish a session inactivity timeout that is as short as possible, based on balancing risk and business
functional requirements. In most cases it should be no more than several hours

clauses.title: Disallow persistent logins and periodically terminate active sessions
clauses.text:
• Disallow persistent logins and enforce periodic session terminations, even when the session is active.
Especially for applications supporting rich network connections or connecting to critical systems.
Termination times should support business requirements and the user should receive sufficient
notification to mitigate negative impacts

clauses.title: Replace prelogin sessions after successful login
clauses.text:
• If a session was established before login, close that session and establish a new session after a
successful login

clauses.title: Regenerate session identifiers on reauthentication
clauses.text: • Generate a new session identifier on any re-authentication

clauses.title: Prohibit concurrent logins with the same user ID
clauses.text: • Do not allow concurrent logins with the same user ID

clauses.title: Expose session identifiers only in HTTP cookie headers
clauses.text:
• Do not expose session identifiers in URLs, error messages or logs. Session identifiers should only be
located in the HTTP cookie header. For example, do not pass session identifiers as GET parameters

clauses.title: Protect server session data with access controls
clauses.text:
• Protect server side session data from unauthorized access, by other users of the server, by
implementing appropriate access controls on the server

clauses.title: Periodically replace and deactivate session identifiers
clauses.text:
• Generate a new session identifier and deactivate the old one periodically. (This can mitigate certain
session hijacking scenarios where the original identifier was compromised)

clauses.title: Regenerate session identifiers when switching to HTTPS
clauses.text:
• Generate a new session identifier if the connection security changes from HTTP to HTTPS, as can
occur during authentication. Within an application, it is recommended to consistently utilize HTTPS
rather than switching between HTTP to HTTPS.

clauses.title: Use per-session random tokens for sensitive operations
clauses.text:
• Supplement standard session management for sensitive server-side operations, like account
management, by utilizing per-session strong random tokens or parameters. This method can be used
to prevent Cross Site Request Forgery attacks

clauses.title: Use per-request random tokens for critical operations
clauses.text:
• Supplement standard session management for highly sensitive or critical operations by utilizing per-
request, as opposed to per-session, strong random tokens or parameters

clauses.title: Set Secure on cookies transmitted over TLS
clauses.text: • Set the "secure" attribute for cookies transmitted over an TLS connection

clauses.title: Set HttpOnly unless scripts require cookie access
clauses.text:
• Set cookies with the HttpOnly attribute, unless you specifically require client-side scripts within your
application to read or set a cookie's value

clauses.title: Access Control
clauses.text: Access Control:

clauses.title: Base authorization decisions on trusted system objects
clauses.text:
• Use only trusted system objects, e.g. server side session objects, for making access authorization
decisions

clauses.title: Centralize sitewide authorization checks
clauses.text:
• Use a single site-wide component to check access authorization. This includes libraries that call
external authorization services

clauses.title: Fail securely in access controls
clauses.text: • Access controls should fail securely

clauses.title: Deny access when security configuration is unavailable
clauses.text: • Deny all access if the application cannot access its security configuration information

clauses.title: Enforce authorization on every request
clauses.text:
• Enforce authorization controls on every request, including those made by server side scripts,
"includes" and requests from rich client-side technologies like AJAX and Flash

clauses.title: Separate privileged logic from other code
clauses.text: • Segregate privileged logic from other application code

clauses.title: Restrict file and resource access to authorized users
clauses.text:
• Restrict access to files or other resources, including those outside the application's direct control, to
only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict protected URLs to authorized users
clauses.text: • Restrict access to protected URLs to only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict protected functions to authorized users
clauses.text: • Restrict access to protected functions to only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict direct object references to authorized users
clauses.text: • Restrict direct object references to only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict service access to authorized users
clauses.text: • Restrict access to services to only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict application data access to authorized users
clauses.text: • Restrict access to application data to only authorized users

clauses.title: Restrict access to authorization attributes and policy information
clauses.text: • Restrict access to user and data attributes and policy information used by access controls

clauses.title: Restrict access to security configuration information
clauses.text: • Restrict access security-relevant configuration information to only authorized users

clauses.title: Match server and presentation access control rules
clauses.text: • Server side implementation and presentation layer representations of access control rules must match

clauses.title: Encrypt client state and verify integrity on the server
clauses.text:
• If state data must be stored on the client, use encryption and integrity checking on the server side to
catch state tampering.

clauses.title: Enforce business rules in application flows
clauses.text: • Enforce application logic flows to comply with business rules

clauses.title: Limit transaction rates per user or device
clauses.text:
• Limit the number of transactions a single user or device can perform in a given period of time. The
transactions/time should be above the actual business requirement, but low enough to deter automated
attacks

clauses.title: Use referer headers only as supplemental authorization checks
clauses.text:
• Use the "referer" header as a supplemental check only, it should never be the sole authorization check,
as it is can be spoofed

clauses.title: Revalidate authorization during long sessions
clauses.text:
• If long authenticated sessions are allowed, periodically re-validate a user’s authorization to ensure that
their privileges have not changed and if they have, log the user out and force them to re-authenticate

clauses.title: Audit accounts and disable unused accounts
clauses.text:
• Implement account auditing and enforce the disabling of unused accounts (e.g., After no more than 30
days from the expiration of an account’s password.)

clauses.title: Disable accounts and terminate sessions when authorization ceases
clauses.text:
• The application must support disabling of accounts and terminating sessions when authorization
ceases (e.g., Changes to role, employment status, business process, etc.)

clauses.title: Apply least privilege to service and integration accounts
clauses.text:
• Service accounts or accounts supporting connections to or from external systems should have the least
privilege possible

clauses.title: Document access requirements in an access control policy
clauses.text:
• Create an Access Control Policy to document an application's business rules, data types and access
authorization criteria and/or processes so that access can be properly provisioned and controlled. This
includes identifying access requirements for both the data and system resources

clauses.title: Cryptographic Practices
clauses.text: Cryptographic Practices:

clauses.title: Implement secret-protecting cryptography on trusted systems
clauses.text:
• All cryptographic functions used to protect secrets from the application user must be implemented on
a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Protect master secrets from unauthorized access
clauses.text: • Protect master secrets from unauthorized access

clauses.title: Fail securely in cryptographic modules
clauses.text: • Cryptographic modules should fail securely

clauses.title: Generate unguessable values with approved cryptographic randomness
clauses.text:
• All random numbers, random file names, random GUIDs, and random strings should be generated
using the cryptographic module’s approved random number generator when these random values are
intended to be un-guessable

clauses.title: Use cryptographic modules compliant with FIPS 140-2 or equivalent
clauses.text:
• Cryptographic modules used by the application should be compliant to FIPS 140-2 or an equivalent
standard. (See http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/STM/cmvp/validation.html)

clauses.title: Establish cryptographic key management policy and processes
clauses.text: • Establish and utilize a policy and process for how cryptographic keys will be managed

clauses.title: Error Handling and Logging
clauses.text: Error Handling and Logging:

clauses.title: Exclude sensitive information from error responses
clauses.text:
• Do not disclose sensitive information in error responses, including system details, session identifiers
or account information

clauses.title: Suppress debugging and stack traces in error handlers
clauses.text: • Use error handlers that do not display debugging or stack trace information

clauses.title: Use generic errors and custom error pages
clauses.text: • Implement generic error messages and use custom error pages

clauses.title: Handle application errors within the application
clauses.text: • The application should handle application errors and not rely on the server configuration

clauses.title: Free allocated memory on errors
clauses.text: • Properly free allocated memory when error conditions occur

clauses.title: Deny access by default on security control errors
clauses.text: • Error handling logic associated with security controls should deny access by default

clauses.title: Implement logging controls on trusted systems
clauses.text: • All logging controls should be implemented on a trusted system (e.g., The server)

clauses.title: Support logging successful and failed security events
clauses.text: • Logging controls should support both success and failure of specified security events

clauses.title: Include important event data in logs
clauses.text: • Ensure logs contain important log event data

clauses.title: Prevent untrusted log data from executing as code
clauses.text:
• Ensure log entries that include un-trusted data will not execute as code in the intended log viewing
interface or software

clauses.title: Restrict log access to authorized individuals
clauses.text: • Restrict access to logs to only authorized individuals

clauses.title: Centralize logging operations
clauses.text: • Utilize a master routine for all logging operations

clauses.title: Exclude sensitive information from logs
clauses.text:
• Do not store sensitive information in logs, including unnecessary system details, session identifiers or
passwords

clauses.title: Provide a log analysis mechanism
clauses.text: • Ensure that a mechanism exists to conduct log analysis

clauses.title: Log all input validation failures
clauses.text: • Log all input validation failures

clauses.title: Log all authentication attempts
clauses.text: • Log all authentication attempts, especially failures

clauses.title: Log all access control failures
clauses.text: • Log all access control failures

clauses.title: Log apparent tampering events
clauses.text: • Log all apparent tampering events, including unexpected changes to state data

clauses.title: Log invalid or expired session token connection attempts
clauses.text: • Log attempts to connect with invalid or expired session tokens

clauses.title: Log all system exceptions
clauses.text: • Log all system exceptions

clauses.title: Log administrative functions and security configuration changes
clauses.text: • Log all administrative functions, including changes to the security configuration settings

clauses.title: Log backend TLS connection failures
clauses.text: • Log all backend TLS connection failures

clauses.title: Log cryptographic module failures
clauses.text: • Log cryptographic module failures

clauses.title: Validate log entry integrity with cryptographic hashes
clauses.text: • Use a cryptographic hash function to validate log entry integrity

clauses.title: Data Protection
clauses.text: Data Protection:

clauses.title: Restrict users to resources needed for their tasks
clauses.text:
• Implement least privilege, restrict users to only the functionality, data and system information that is
required to perform their tasks

clauses.title: Protect and promptly purge temporary sensitive data
clauses.text:
• Protect all cached or temporary copies of sensitive data stored on the server from unauthorized access
and purge those temporary working files a soon as they are no longer required.

clauses.title: Encrypt highly sensitive stored information using vetted algorithms
clauses.text:
• Encrypt highly sensitive stored information, like authentication verification data, even on the server
side. Always use well vetted algorithms, see "Cryptographic Practices" for additional guidance

clauses.title: Prevent users from downloading server source code
clauses.text: • Protect server-side source-code from being downloaded by a user

clauses.title: Prevent insecure client storage of sensitive information
clauses.text:
• Do not store passwords, connection strings or other sensitive information in clear text or in any non-
cryptographically secure manner on the client side. This includes embedding in insecure formats like:
MS viewstate, Adobe flash or compiled code

clauses.title: Remove sensitive comments from accessible production code
clauses.text:
• Remove comments in user accessible production code that may reveal backend system or other
sensitive information

clauses.title: Remove unnecessary application and system documentation
clauses.text:
• Remove unnecessary application and system documentation as this can reveal useful information to
attackers

clauses.title: Exclude sensitive information from HTTP GET parameters
clauses.text: • Do not include sensitive information in HTTP GET request parameters

clauses.title: Disable autocomplete on sensitive forms
clauses.text:
• Disable auto complete features on forms expected to contain sensitive information, including
authentication

clauses.title: Disable client caching of sensitive pages
clauses.text:
• Disable client side caching on pages containing sensitive information. Cache-Control: no-store, may
be used in conjunction with the HTTP header control "Pragma: no-cache", which is less effective, but
is HTTP/1.0 backward compatible

clauses.title: Support removal of sensitive data no longer needed
clauses.text:
• The application should support the removal of sensitive data when that data is no longer required.
(e.g. personal information or certain financial data)

clauses.title: Control access to sensitive server data
clauses.text:
• Implement appropriate access controls for sensitive data stored on the server. This includes cached
data, temporary files and data that should be accessible only by specific system users

clauses.title: Communication Security
clauses.text: Communication Security:

clauses.title: Encrypt transmission of all sensitive information
clauses.text:
• Implement encryption for the transmission of all sensitive information. This should include TLS for
protecting the connection and may be supplemented by discrete encryption of sensitive files or non-
HTTP based connections

clauses.title: Use valid TLS certificates with required intermediate certificates
clauses.text:
• TLS certificates should be valid and have the correct domain name, not be expired, and be installed
with intermediate certificates when required

clauses.title: Prevent insecure fallback after TLS failures
clauses.text: • Failed TLS connections should not fall back to an insecure connection

clauses.title: Use TLS for authenticated and sensitive content
clauses.text:
• Utilize TLS connections for all content requiring authenticated access and for all other sensitive
information

clauses.title: Use TLS for sensitive external system connections
clauses.text: • Utilize TLS for connections to external systems that involve sensitive information or functions

clauses.title: Use a single appropriately configured TLS implementation
clauses.text: • Utilize a single standard TLS implementation that is configured appropriately

clauses.title: Specify character encodings for all connections
clauses.text: • Specify character encodings for all connections

clauses.title: Remove sensitive parameters from external link referers
clauses.text:
• Filter parameters containing sensitive information from the HTTP referer, when linking to external
sites

clauses.title: System Configuration
clauses.text: System Configuration:

clauses.title: Run the latest approved system component versions
clauses.text: • Ensure servers, frameworks and system components are running the latest approved version

clauses.title: Apply all patches for component versions in use
clauses.text: • Ensure servers, frameworks and system components have all patches issued for the version in use

clauses.title: Disable directory listings
clauses.text: • Turn off directory listings

clauses.title: Minimize web server, process, and service account privileges
clauses.text: • Restrict the web server, process and service accounts to the least privileges possible

clauses.title: Fail securely when exceptions occur
clauses.text: • When exceptions occur, fail securely

clauses.title: Remove unnecessary functionality and files
clauses.text: • Remove all unnecessary functionality and files

clauses.title: Remove test code and nonproduction functionality before deployment
clauses.text: • Remove test code or any functionality not intended for production, prior to deployment

clauses.title: Avoid disclosing directory structure through robots.txt
clauses.text:
• Prevent disclosure of your directory structure in the robots.txt file by placing directories not intended
for public indexing into an isolated parent directory. Then "Disallow" that entire parent directory in
the robots.txt file rather than Disallowing each individual directory

clauses.title: Define supported HTTP methods and page handling
clauses.text:
• Define which HTTP methods, Get or Post, the application will support and whether it will be handled
differently in different pages in the application

clauses.title: Disable unnecessary HTTP methods and authenticate file handling extensions
clauses.text:
• Disable unnecessary HTTP methods, such as WebDAV extensions. If an extended HTTP method that
supports file handling is required, utilize a well-vetted authentication mechanism

clauses.title: Align HTTP 1.0 and 1.1 configurations or understand differences
clauses.text:
• If the web server handles both HTTP 1.0 and 1.1, ensure that both are configured in a similar manor
or insure that you understand any difference that may exist (e.g. handling of extended HTTP methods)

clauses.title: Remove unnecessary system details from HTTP response headers
clauses.text:
• Remove unnecessary information from HTTP response headers related to the OS, web-server version
and application frameworks

clauses.title: Support human readable security configuration output
clauses.text:
• The security configuration store for the application should be able to be output in human readable
form to support auditing

clauses.title: Register system components and software in asset management
clauses.text: • Implement an asset management system and register system components and software in it

clauses.title: Isolate development environments and restrict access
clauses.text:
• Isolate development environments from the production network and provide access only to authorized
development and test groups. Development environments are often configured less securely than
production environments and attackers may use this difference to discover shared weaknesses or as an
avenue for exploitation

clauses.title: Manage and record code changes through change control
clauses.text:
• Implement a software change control system to manage and record changes to the code both
in development and production

clauses.title: Database Security
clauses.text: Database Security:

clauses.title: Use strongly typed parameterized queries
clauses.text: • Use strongly typed parameterized queries

clauses.title: Validate and encode database inputs before executing commands
clauses.text:
• Utilize input validation and output encoding and be sure to address meta characters. If these fail, do
not run the database command

clauses.title: Use strongly typed variables
clauses.text: • Ensure that variables are strongly typed

clauses.title: Minimize application database privileges
clauses.text: • The application should use the lowest possible level of privilege when accessing the database

clauses.title: Use secure database credentials
clauses.text: • Use secure credentials for database access

clauses.title: Store encrypted connection strings separately on trusted systems
clauses.text:
• Connection strings should not be hard coded within the application. Connection strings should be
stored in a separate configuration file on a trusted system and they should be encrypted.

clauses.title: Abstract data access through stored procedures
clauses.text:
• Use stored procedures to abstract data access and allow for the removal of permissions to the base
tables in the database

clauses.title: Close database connections promptly
clauses.text: • Close the connection as soon as possible

clauses.title: Replace default database administrator passwords with strong authentication
clauses.text:
• Remove or change all default database administrative passwords. Utilize strong passwords/phrases or
implement multi-factor authentication

clauses.title: Disable unnecessary database functionality
clauses.text:
• Turn off all unnecessary database functionality (e.g., unnecessary stored procedures or services, utility
packages, install only the minimum set of features and options required (surface area reduction))

clauses.title: Remove unnecessary default database content
clauses.text: • Remove unnecessary default vendor content (e.g., sample schemas)

clauses.title: Disable unnecessary default database accounts
clauses.text: • Disable any default accounts that are not required to support business requirements

clauses.title: Use distinct database credentials for each trust distinction
clauses.text:
• The application should connect to the database with different credentials for every trust distinction
(e.g., user, read-only user, guest, administrators)

clauses.title: File Management
clauses.text: File Management:

clauses.title: Prohibit direct user data in dynamic includes
clauses.text: • Do not pass user supplied data directly to any dynamic include function

clauses.title: Require authentication before file uploads
clauses.text: • Require authentication before allowing a file to be uploaded

clauses.title: Limit uploads to necessary file types
clauses.text: • Limit the type of files that can be uploaded to only those types that are needed for business purposes

clauses.title: Validate uploaded file types using file headers
clauses.text:
• Validate uploaded files are the expected type by checking file headers. Checking for file type by
extension alone is not sufficient

clauses.title: Store files outside the application web context
clauses.text:
• Do not save files in the same web context as the application. Files should either go to the content
server or in the database.

clauses.title: Restrict uploads of files interpretable by the web server
clauses.text: • Prevent or restrict the uploading of any file that may be interpreted by the web server.

clauses.title: Disable execution in upload directories
clauses.text: • Turn off execution privileges on file upload directories

clauses.title: Use logical drives or chroot environments for UNIX uploads
clauses.text:
• Implement safe uploading in UNIX by mounting the targeted file directory as a logical drive using the
associated path or the chrooted environment

clauses.title: Validate file references against allowed names and types
clauses.text:
• When referencing existing files, use a white list of allowed file names and types. Validate the value of
the parameter being passed and if it does not match one of the expected values, either reject it or use a
hard coded default file value for the content instead

clauses.title: Restrict dynamic redirects to validated relative URLs
clauses.text:
• Do not pass user supplied data into a dynamic redirect. If this must be allowed, then the redirect
should accept only validated, relative path URLs

clauses.title: Use mapped indexes instead of file or directory paths
clauses.text: • Do not pass directory or file paths, use index values mapped to pre-defined list of paths

clauses.title: Never send absolute file paths to clients
clauses.text: • Never send the absolute file path to the client

clauses.title: Make application files and resources read-only
clauses.text: • Ensure application files and resources are read-only

clauses.title: Scan uploaded files for viruses and malware
clauses.text: • Scan user uploaded files for viruses and malware

clauses.title: Memory Management
clauses.text: Memory Management:

clauses.title: Control input and output of untrusted data
clauses.text: • Utilize input and output control for un-trusted data

clauses.title: Verify specified buffer sizes
clauses.text: • Double check that the buffer is as large as specified

clauses.title: Account for missing NULL termination in bounded copies
clauses.text:
• When using functions that accept a number of bytes to copy, such as strncpy(), be aware that if the
destination buffer size is equal to the source buffer size, it may not NULL-terminate the string

clauses.title: Check buffer boundaries during looped function calls
clauses.text:
• Check buffer boundaries if calling the function in a loop and make sure there is no danger of writing
past the allocated space

clauses.title: Truncate strings before copying or concatenating
clauses.text:
• Truncate all input strings to a reasonable length before passing them to the copy and concatenation
functions

clauses.title: Explicitly close resources
clauses.text:
• Specifically close resources, don’t rely on garbage collection. (e.g., connection objects, file handles,
etc.)

clauses.title: Use non-executable stacks when available
clauses.text: • Use non-executable stacks when available

clauses.title: Avoid known vulnerable functions
clauses.text: • Avoid the use of known vulnerable functions (e.g., printf, strcat, strcpy etc.)

clauses.title: Free allocated memory at function completion and all exits
clauses.text: • Properly free allocated memory upon the completion of functions and at all exit points

clauses.title: General Coding Practices
clauses.text: General Coding Practices:

clauses.title: Use tested approved managed code for common tasks
clauses.text: • Use tested and approved managed code rather than creating new unmanaged code for common tasks

clauses.title: Use task specific APIs for operating system tasks
clauses.text:
• Utilize task specific built-in APIs to conduct operating system tasks. Do not allow the application to
issue commands directly to the Operating System, especially through the use of application initiated
command shells

clauses.title: Verify code and configuration integrity using checksums or hashes
clauses.text:
• Use checksums or hashes to verify the integrity of interpreted code, libraries, executables, and
configuration files

clauses.title: Prevent race conditions through locking or synchronization
clauses.text:
• Utilize locking to prevent multiple simultaneous requests or use a synchronization mechanism to
prevent race conditions

clauses.title: Protect shared variables and resources from inappropriate concurrent access
clauses.text: • Protect shared variables and resources from inappropriate concurrent access

clauses.title: Explicitly initialize variables and data stores before use
clauses.text:
• Explicitly initialize all your variables and other data stores, either during declaration or just before the
first usage

clauses.title: Minimize duration of elevated privileges
clauses.text:
• In cases where the application must run with elevated privileges, raise privileges as late as possible,
and drop them as soon as possible

clauses.title: Prevent calculation errors arising from numeric representations
clauses.text:
• Avoid calculation errors by understanding your programming language's underlying representation
and how it interacts with numeric calculation. Pay close attention to byte size discrepancies, precision,
signed/unsigned distinctions, truncation, conversion and casting between types, "not-a-number"
calculations, and how your language handles numbers that are too large or too small for its underlying
representation

clauses.title: Prohibit user data in dynamic execution functions
clauses.text: • Do not pass user supplied data to any dynamic execution function

clauses.title: Restrict users from creating or modifying code
clauses.text: • Restrict users from generating new code or altering existing code

clauses.title: Review third party components for necessity and safety
clauses.text:
• Review all secondary applications, third party code and libraries to determine business necessity and
validate safe functionality, as these can introduce new vulnerabilities

clauses.title: Secure updates with verified signatures and encrypted transfers
clauses.text:
• Implement safe updating. If the application will utilize automatic updates, then use cryptographic
signatures for your code and ensure your download clients verify those signatures. Use encrypted
channels to transfer the code from the host server

clauses.title: Appendix B: Glossary
clauses.text: Appendix B: Glossary

clauses.title: Definition of abuse case
clauses.text:
Abuse Case: Describes the intentional and unintentional misuses of the software. Abuse cases should
challenge the assumptions of the system design.

clauses.title: Definition of access control
clauses.text:
Access Control: A set of controls that grant or deny a user, or other entity, access to a system resource. This
is usually based on hierarchical roles and individual privileges within a role, but also includes system to
system interactions.

clauses.title: Definition of authentication
clauses.text:
Authentication: A set of controls that are used to verify the identity of a user, or other entity, interacting
with the software.

clauses.title: Definition of availability
clauses.text: Availability: A measure of a system's accessibility and usability.

clauses.title: Definition of canonicalize
clauses.text: Canonicalize: To reduce various encodings and representations of data to a single simple form.

clauses.title: Definition of communication security
clauses.text:
Communication Security: A set of controls that help ensure the software handles the sending and receiving
of information in a secure manner.

clauses.title: Definition of confidentiality
clauses.text: Confidentiality: To ensure that information is disclosed only to authorized parties.

clauses.title: Definition of contextual output encoding
clauses.text:
Contextual Output Encoding: Encoding output data based on how it will be utilized by the application. The
specific methods vary depending on the way the output data is used. If the data is to be included in the
response to the client, account for inclusion scenarios like: the body of an HTML document, an HTML
attribute, within JavaScript, within a CSS or in a URL. You must also account for other use cases like SQL
queries, XML and LDAP.

clauses.title: Definition of cross site request forgery
clauses.text:
Cross Site Request Forgery: An external website or application forces a client to make an unintended
request to another application that the client has an active session with. Applications are vulnerable when
they use known, or predictable, URLs and parameters; and when the browser automatically transmits all
required session information with each request to the vulnerable application. (This is one of the only attacks
specifically discussed in this document and is only included because the associated vulnerability is very
common and poorly understood.)

clauses.title: Definition of cryptographic practices
clauses.text:
Cryptographic Practices: A set of controls that ensure cryptographic operations within the application are
handled securely.

clauses.title: Definition of data protection
clauses.text:
Data Protection: A set of controls that help ensure the software handles the storing of information in a
secure manner.

clauses.title: Definition of database security
clauses.text:
Database Security: A set of controls that ensure that software interacts with a database in a secure manner
and that the database is configured securely.

clauses.title: Definition of error handling and logging
clauses.text:
Error Handling and Logging: A set of practices that ensure the application handles errors safely and
conducts proper event logging.

clauses.title: Definition of exploit
clauses.text:
Exploit: To take advantage of a vulnerability. Typically this is an intentional action designed to compromise
the software's security controls by leveraging a vulnerability.

clauses.title: Definition of file management
clauses.text: File Management: A set of controls that cover the interaction between the code and other system files.

clauses.title: Definition of general coding practices
clauses.text:
General Coding Practices: A set of controls that cover coding practices that do not fit easily into other
categories.

clauses.title: Definition of hazardous character
clauses.text:
Hazardous Character: Any character or encoded representation of a character that can effect the intended
operation of the application or associated system by being interpreted to have a special meaning, outside the
intended use of the character. These characters may be used to:
• Altering the structure of existing code or statements
• Inserting new unintended code
• Altering paths
• Causing unexpected outcomes from program functions or routines
• Causing error conditions
• Having any of the above effects on down stream applications or systems

clauses.title: Definition of HTML entity encoding
clauses.text:
HTML Entity Encode: The process of replacing certain ASCII characters with their HTML entity
equivalents. For example, encoding would replace the less than character "<" with the HTML equivalent
"<". HTML entities are 'inert' in most interpreters, especially browsers, which can mitigate certain client
side attacks.

clauses.title: Definition of impact
clauses.text:
Impact: A measure of the negative effect to the business that results from the occurrence of an undesired
event; what would be the result of a vulnerability being exploited.

clauses.title: Definition of input validation
clauses.text:
Input Validation: A set of controls that verify the properties of all input data matches what is expected by
the application including types, lengths, ranges, acceptable character sets and does not include known
hazardous characters.

clauses.title: Definition of integrity
clauses.text:
Integrity: The assurance that information is accurate, complete and valid, and has not been altered by an
unauthorized action.

clauses.title: Definition of log event data
clauses.text:
Log Event Data: This should include the following:
1. Time stamp from a trusted system component
2. Severity rating for each event
3. Tagging of security relevant events, if they are mixed with other log entries
4. Identity of the account/user that caused the event
5. Source IP address associated with the request
6. Event outcome (success or failure)
7. Description of the event

clauses.title: Definition of memory management
clauses.text: Memory Management: A set of controls that address memory and buffer usage.

clauses.title: Definition of mitigate
clauses.text:
Mitigate: Steps taken to reduce the severity of a vulnerability. These can include removing a vulnerability,
making a vulnerability more difficult to exploit, or reducing the negative impact of a successful exploitation.

clauses.title: Definition of multifactor authentication
clauses.text:
Multi-Factor Authentication: An authentication process that requires the user to produce multiple distinct
types of credentials. Typically this is based on something they have (e.g., smartcard), something they know
(e.g., a pin), or something they are (e.g., data from a biometric reader).

clauses.title: Definition of output encoding
clauses.text:
Output Encoding: A set of controls addressing the use of encoding to ensure data output by the application
is safe.

clauses.title: Definition of parameterized queries
clauses.text:
Parameterized Queries (prepared statements): Keeps the query and data separate through the use of
placeholders. The query structure is defined with place holders, the SQL statement is sent to the database and
prepared, and then the prepared statement is combined with the parameter values. The prevents the query
from being altered, because the parameter values are combined with the compiled statement, not a SQL
string.

clauses.title: Definition of sanitize data
clauses.text:
Sanitize Data: The process of making potentially harmful data safe through the use of data removal,
replacement, encoding or escaping of the characters.

clauses.title: Definition of security controls
clauses.text:
Security Controls: An action that mitigates a potential vulnerability and helps ensure that the software
behaves only in the expected manner.

clauses.title: Definition of security requirements
clauses.text:
Security Requirements: A set of design and functional requirements that help ensure the software is built
and deployed in a secure manner.

clauses.title: Definition of sequential authentication
clauses.text:
Sequential Authentication: When authentication data is requested on successive pages rather than being
requested all at once on a single page.

clauses.title: Definition of session management
clauses.text:
Session Management: A set of controls that help ensure web applications handle HTTP sessions in a secure
manner.

clauses.title: Definition of state data
clauses.text:
State Data: When data or parameters are used, by the application or server, to emulate a persistent
connection or track a client's status across a multi-request process or transaction.

clauses.title: Definition of system
clauses.text:
System: A generic term covering the operating systems, web server, application frameworks and related
infrastructure.

clauses.title: Definition of system configuration
clauses.text:
System Configuration: A set of controls that help ensure the infrastructure components supporting the
software are deployed securely.

clauses.title: Definition of threat agent
clauses.text:
Threat Agent: Any entity which may have a negative impact on the system. This may be a malicious user
who wants to compromise the system's security controls; however, it could also be an accidental misuse of
the system or a more physical threat like fire or flood.

clauses.title: Definition of trust boundaries
clauses.text:
Trust Boundaries: Typically a trust boundary constitutes the components of the system under your direct
control. All connections and data from systems outside of your direct control, including all clients and
systems managed by other parties, should be consider untrusted and be validated at the boundary, before
allowing further system interaction.

clauses.title: Definition of vulnerability
clauses.text: Vulnerability: A weakness that makes the system susceptible to attack or damage.

checks.summary: Make the work's Creative Commons Attribution ShareAlike 3.0 license terms clear to recipients whenever it is reused or distributed.
checks.why: Disclosure during reuse or distribution is a process obligation that source code and configuration cannot establish.
checks.question: Whenever this work is reused or distributed, are its Creative Commons Attribution ShareAlike 3.0 license terms made clear to recipients?

checks.summary: Assess secure software development lifecycle maturity and development staff knowledge when starting to use the guide.
checks.why: These assessments concern organisational practices and staff knowledge.
checks.question: When starting to use the guide, did the team assess both its secure software development lifecycle maturity and its development staff's knowledge?

checks.summary: Ensure developers have the knowledge or guidance resources needed to implement the coding practices.
checks.why: Developer knowledge and access to adequate guidance cannot be established from application source code.
checks.question: Do developers have either the prior knowledge or sufficient guidance resources needed to implement the guide's coding practices?

checks.summary: Assign other development team members responsibility for validating the security of the entire system's design and implementation.
checks.why: Assignment of validation responsibilities is an organisational obligation.
checks.question: Are other development team members assigned responsibility for validating the security of the entire system's design and implementation?

checks.summary: Provide security validators with adequate training, tools, and resources.
checks.why: The adequacy of personnel training and available validation resources requires organisational evidence.
checks.question: Do the team members responsible for security validation have adequate training, tools, and resources to validate the entire system's design and implementation?

checks.summary: Clearly define roles and responsibilities.
checks.why: Team roles and responsibilities are organisational assignments.
checks.question: Are roles and responsibilities clearly defined?

checks.summary: Provide development teams with adequate software security training.
checks.why: Training provision and adequacy cannot be established from application source code.
checks.question: Have development teams been provided with adequate software security training?

checks.summary: Implement a secure software development lifecycle.
checks.why: A development lifecycle is an organisational process.
checks.question: Has a secure software development lifecycle been implemented?

checks.summary: Establish secure coding standards.
checks.why: Establishing standards is a policy obligation.
checks.question: Have secure coding standards been established?

checks.summary: Provide a reusable object library.
checks.why: A reviewer can inspect the source for a reusable library, but no supplied fact represents it.

checks.summary: Verify the effectiveness of security controls.
checks.why: Performing effectiveness verification requires evidence of validation activities and results.
checks.question: Has the effectiveness of the system's security controls been verified?

checks.summary: Establish secure outsourced development practices.
checks.why: Outsourced development practices are organisational processes.
checks.question: Where development is outsourced, have secure outsourced development practices been established?

checks.summary: Define security requirements and verification methodologies in both outsourced development RFPs and contracts.
checks.why: RFP and contract contents require procurement and contractual evidence.
checks.question: Where development is outsourced, do both the RFP and contract define security requirements and verification methodologies?

checks.summary: Perform all required data validation on a trusted system.
checks.why: A reviewer can trace validation execution and trust boundaries, but the supplied facts do not describe them.

checks.summary: Identify all data sources and classify each as trusted or untrusted.
checks.why: A reviewer can inspect data ingress and its trust classification in source and configuration; no supplied fact captures this.

checks.summary: Validate all data received from untrusted sources, including databases and file streams.
checks.why: The supplied facts do not capture general validation of data from every untrusted source.

checks.summary: Provide a centralized input validation routine for the application.
checks.why: Validation centralization is visible in application structure but is not represented by the supplied facts.

checks.summary: Specify an appropriate character set, such as UTF-8, for every input source.
checks.why: The facts do not describe input character set declarations.

checks.summary: Convert input to a common character set before validating it.
checks.why: The facts do not capture character set conversion or validation order.

checks.summary: Reject input whenever validation fails.
checks.why: The facts do not capture validation failure handling.

checks.summary: Determine whether UTF-8 extended characters are supported and, if supported, validate input only after UTF-8 decoding completes.
checks.why: Source code and configuration can show UTF-8 support and decoding order, but the facts do not capture them.

checks.summary: Validate all client-provided data before processing, including parameters, URLs, headers, cookies, and automated submissions from embedded code.
checks.why: The facts do not describe validation coverage or its order relative to processing.

checks.summary: Verify that request and response header values contain only ASCII characters.
checks.why: The facts do not capture header character validation.

checks.summary: Validate data at redirect targets even when requests bypass validation performed before the redirect.
checks.why: The facts do not capture redirect target validation.

checks.summary: Validate input against its expected data type.
checks.why: The facts do not capture input type validation.

checks.summary: Validate input values against their permitted ranges.
checks.why: The facts do not capture general input range constraints.
